title: The Power of Habit: 10 things to do

slides.title: Why Your New Habits Never _Stick_ (And 10 Fixes)
Most Of Your Day Isn't A Decision
body: A Duke study Duhigg cites suggests **more than 40%** of daily actions are habits.
That's why willpower alone keeps losing. These 10 moves work *with* the autopilot.

slides.title: Watch One Ordinary Hour
body: Tally every move you **didn't decide** to make.
You can't change a pattern you *can't see.*

slides.title: Map One Habit As A Loop
body: Every habit is a **cue**, a **routine** and a **reward**, repeated until it runs itself.
Pick one habit and fill in all three.

slides.title: When The Urge Hits, Ask 5 Questions
body: Cues almost always hide in one of these five.
Note them each time. Duhigg found his cookie urge struck at **3:30, every day.**

slides.title: Test What You're Really Craving
body: Swap the reward for a few days. After each, write **3 words** on how you feel.
Still want the old thing *15 minutes later?* If not, you've found the real reward.

slides.title: Keep The Cue And Reward. Swap The Routine.
body: This is the **Golden Rule** of habit change.
You can't delete a habit. But you can *re-route* it, and the craving still gets fed.

slides.title: Give New Habits A Reward To Crave

graphic.note: pair it, repeat it, and your brain starts expecting it

body: New habits stick when your brain **looks forward** to something.
A treat, a tick on a chart, a moment of pride. *Same reward, every time.*

slides.title: Find One Person Who Believes You Can

graphic.q: Who's still going when life gets hard?

body: In recovery groups, people who **believed** they could change were more likely to stay sober when life got hard.
Belief grows in groups. Start with *one person.*

slides.title: Start One Keystone Habit
body: Some habits set off a **chain reaction**. When people start exercising, other habits often improve too.
Which one habit could *tip the rest?*

slides.title: Plan Your Weak Moment In Advance

items.will: walk over and chat for 10 minutes.

graphic.note: Write yours. Decide now, not in the moment.

body: Willpower fails **at the worst moment**. Starbucks trains staff with plans for exactly those moments.
A plan turns a stressful cue into a *ready-made routine.*

slides.title: Rehearse It Until It's Automatic
body: Run the plan in your head, then for real, **again and again.**
Willpower is a muscle that tires. A rehearsed habit *doesn't need it.*

slides.title: Which One Will You Try This Week?

graphic.q: Pick one of the 10 and start it today. Which one?

body: Change one loop. Then the next. **That's how habits really change.**
